# netsim

## Maturity

**Grade:** 3 · S3 E2 A2 H– P3 · limited by scope (core), performance (not measured) *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** core — tokio-rs/turmoil 0.7.2, TigerBeetle VOPR methodology, protocol-level; real `std.Io` code and disk faults are the sibling `simio` (surveyed 2026-10-05)

**Audit:** review 2026-09-15 · mutation 2026-09-10 · src ?

**Hardening:** fuzz n/a — no fuzz obligation under check-fuzz (initial v2 fill, not reviewed) · ct n/a — network simulation (keyword review, 2026-10-08)

**Performance:** not measured

**Evidence:** model — determinism (same seed identical) and invariant hook with shrinking; harness itself, no external model

**Known defects:** none recorded

**Downstream consumer:** no

A **deterministic, seeded, discrete-event network simulator** — the harness that
model-checks distributed algorithms. A topology of nodes and directed links
(per-link latency / jitter / loss / duplication / reorder / bandwidth, per-node
clock skew) is driven by a seeded PRNG through a single time-ordered event queue
with deterministic tie-breaking, so **every run is a pure function of its seed
and replays byte-for-byte**.

On top of the engine sits the adversary: a seeded failure-schedule fuzzer (link
up/down, arbitrary-cut partitions and heals, message drop / duplicate / delay
spike, node crash and restart, clock jumps), caller-registered invariant
predicates checked after *every* event, byte-exact replay of a concrete trace,
and a delta-debugging (ddmin) counterexample minimizer.

This is the VOPR methodology already proven in [`kv`](../kv), generalized from a
single store to a network. netsim itself bakes in **no** protocol specifics: an
algorithm plugs in as a `Protocol` consumer — see [`raft`](../raft),
[`loopfree-reconv`](../loopfree-reconv), [`df-elect`](../df-elect) and
[`liveness-hyst`](../liveness-hyst).

**Not here, by design — use [`simio`](../simio):** running *unmodified* code
written against `std.Io` (sockets, clocks, tasks, files) under simulation, and
storage faults (lost/torn unsynced writes, bit rot, disk I/O errors). `simio`
is built on netsim — its seeded PRNG, its fault-schedule generator and its
`ddmin` shrinker — and keeps netsim pure and platform-free (decided 2026-10-01,
see `simio`'s SPEC "Why this module exists"). Pick netsim when the algorithm
is (or can be written as) a message-passing state machine; pick `simio` when
the code under test already talks to `std.Io`.

- **Status:** the main use case — model-checking a distributed algorithm under
  network, crash and clock faults with replay and minimization — is done and
  drives 7 in-repo protocol consumers (and `simio`); the remaining gaps are under
  [Backlog / deferred](#backlog--deferred). **Platform:** any — pure simulation, no OS or network
  I/O, no wall-clock read.
- **Deps:** none (std only).
- **Model after:** TigerBeetle's VOPR / deterministic discrete-event network
  simulation.

**Where we are ahead:** in one dependency-free, platform-free Zig library: a seeded
fault-schedule fuzzer (link up/down, arbitrary-cut partitions and heals, one-shot
drop/duplicate/delay, crash/restart, clock jumps) over per-link loss/dup/jitter/reorder/
bandwidth, invariants checked after *every* event, byte-exact replay, and a ddmin
counterexample minimizer — no turmoil, marionette or madsim README mentions a shrinker
(verified for turmoil and marionette 2026-10-05). Runs on any target, including
32-bit, with no OS I/O. **Where we are even:** with VOPR/FoundationDB's method for a
message-passing algorithm. **Not here, by design (→ `simio`):** running real `std.Io`
code (turmoil-net, marionette, Shadow, madsim's route) and storage faults (turmoil-fs,
marionette's disk, VOPR's storage) — `simio` provides both on top of netsim's
generator and shrinker. **Where we are behind (→ Backlog):** no message-corruption
fault kind (`rg -i corrupt src/` finds none; `simio` flips datagram bits only for real
`std.Io` code); safety-only search — a liveness property ("a leader is elected after the
heal") is checked by hand after `run` (see `raft`'s `server.zig`), not by
`findFailing`/`shrinkTrace`; no consistency/history checker like Maelstrom's (consumers
write invariants); a protocol is not told about a crash, so durable-vs-volatile state
across `crash_node`/`restart_node` is each consumer's own bookkeeping.

**Re-surveyed 2026-10-05 (mvp → core).** The 2026-09-30 card's "behind" list — no
real-code interposition, no storage-fault model — predated the sibling `simio`
(2026-10-01, `core`), which this README did not mention. Those two are now a deliberate
split, not gaps: the user decided netsim stays a pure protocol-level engine and the
`std.Io`/disk layer lives in `simio`, which reuses netsim's generator and ddmin
(verified in `simio/src/search.zig`). Judged as a module on its own contract, netsim
covers the main use case — model-checking a message-passing algorithm under network,
crash and clock faults with replay and minimization — for 7 in-repo consumers; what is
left is Backlog-grade (each has a workaround). Not `parity`: Maelstrom's history
checkers and a liveness search are things a user can notice missing.

## Use

```zig
const netsim = @import("netsim");

// 1. Topology.
fn scenario(sim: *netsim.Sim) anyerror!void {
    for (0..5) |_| _ = try sim.addNode(.{});
    try sim.addBiLink(0, 1, .{ .latency = 10, .loss_permille = 10 });
}

// 2. Algorithm as a Protocol (onStart / onMessage / onTimer / check), then
//    fuzz a fault schedule across a seed range; null == every seed held.
const case = netsim.Case{ .seed = 0, .scenario = scenario, .protocol = p, .until = 2000 };
const failing = try netsim.findFailing(gpa, case, .{}, 1, 300);

// 3. Minimize whatever it found, and replay it deterministically.
if (failing) |f| {
    var min = try netsim.shrinkTrace(gpa, &f);   // .before / .after event counts
    defer min.deinit();
    _ = try netsim.replay(gpa, case, min.trace.events, null);
}
```

`run` fuzzes one seed and returns `.ok` or `.violated` with the exact
`FaultTrace` reproducer; `replay` re-runs a concrete trace as a deterministic
oracle; `findFailing` + `shrink` search a seed range and minimize.

## Verify

```
scripts/modtest netsim    # Debug with LLVM; last recorded 49/49 (2026-09-11)
```

The determinism property is the load-bearing one and is tested directly: the
same seed produces an identical event log, and a replayed trace reproduces the
violation it was minimized from. Consumers add their own invariants — a
harness with no teeth is the failure mode this module exists to avoid, so each
consumer ships a deliberately-broken positive control that MUST trip its
checker (see `raft`'s `BrokenRaft`).

Provenance: original work of the zig-libs authors (MIT) — the deterministic
seeded discrete-event simulator, the failure-schedule fuzzer, the byte-exact
replay oracle and the ddmin counterexample minimizer. The METHODOLOGY — a
simulator that is a pure function of its seed, driving a real implementation
under a fuzzed fault schedule with invariants checked after every event —
follows TigerBeetle's VOPR (**Apache-2.0**), a **design reference only**: no
TigerBeetle source was consulted or copied, and this module's engine, event
queue and API are unrelated to it. The splitmix64 mixer is Sebastiano Vigna's
public-domain algorithm. The methodology is borrowed from this repo's own `kv`
VOPR, not its code.

## Backlog / deferred

- **Message-corruption fault kind (bit flips / truncation on a link)** (survey 2026-09-30, still open 2026-10-05): `FaultKind` has drop, duplicate, delay, cut and crash but no byte-level damage; a codec-carrying protocol wants it. `simio`'s `corrupt_permille` covers only real `std.Io` datagrams. Effort S (a `corrupt_once` kind plus a `LinkConfig.corrupt_permille`, with the shrinker seeing it like any other fault). Fits §2.
- **End-of-run (liveness) predicate in the search** (survey 2026-10-05): `checkFn` runs after every event, so only safety properties reach `findFailing`/`shrinkTrace`; "eventually X after the network heals" is checked by hand after `run` (`raft/src/server.zig`'s liveness tests), and such a failure cannot be minimized. Effort S (an optional `Protocol.finalFn` evaluated at `until`, reported as a violation). Fits §2.
- **Crash notification for durable-vs-volatile state** (survey 2026-10-05): `crash_node` stops a node silently and `restart_node` re-runs `onStart`; what survives is each consumer's own bookkeeping (`raft`'s `Node` restarts from its persisted state). An optional `onCrashFn` hook would let a protocol drop volatile state at the crash instant. Effort S. Fits §2.
- ~~**Storage-fault model (torn/lost/misdirected writes, crash mid-write)**~~ (survey 2026-09-30) — **done elsewhere, by design, 2026-10-01:** `simio` gives each host a crash-consistent disk (unsynced data lost, kept or torn per 512-byte sector; directory-sync durability) plus one-shot disk I/O errors and bit rot in its fault search, built on netsim's generator and ddmin. netsim stays protocol-level; a store or WAL under test runs on `simio`.
- **Deliberately not here — real-code interposition** (survey 2026-10-05): sockets, clocks, tasks and files under simulation are `simio`'s job (user decision 2026-10-01, netsim stays pure and platform-free).

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class C · oracle n/a

- **Class C** — internal algorithm or data structure — no outside exists, so correctness is defined by invariants or a brute-force reference. Not anchor debt.
- **Oracle n/a** — class C/D carries no anchor debt, so there is no oracle grade to give.

**What the tests actually contain.** in-process deterministic sim/test harness, no wire; correctness = determinism/invariants
